newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 22.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Thursday:
* Stock prices were mixed as investors continued to worry about how the Fed might act on interest rates.
* The U.S. trade deficit fell in March to $8.5 billion from $10.5 billion February.
* The president of Wells Fargo and Co has decided to retire.
* Household International Inc has acquired the consumer finance business of Transamerica Corp for $1.1 billion.
* Toyota Motor Corp's earnings were up but fell short of analysts' expectations.
* Toy Biz Inc has reached an agreement with Marvel that would give Toy Biz 40 percent of the restructured company.
* A panel of computer experts said the U.S. plan to pursue criminals on the Internet via data-scrambling software could increase security risks.
* Tyco International is gobbling up companies at a time when many companies would rather trim than expand.
* The Connecticut General Assembly has voted to restrict the power of managed-care companies seeking to deny treatment for patients.
* Private lawyers are increasing their influence in the states' battle against the tobacco industry.
* The Marriott hotel's decision a few years ago to set up shop in Times Square in New York is paying off as the area turns around.
* The Metropolitan Transportation Authority of New York City has delayed acting on a $95 million-contract for Lockheed Martin .
* Club Med is looking at new marketing alliances.
* Despite deregulation of the local telephone market, monopolies still rule the U.S. market.
* LG&E Energy has an agreement to acquire KU Energy for $1.5 billion in stock.
* The Clinton administration has introduced a plan to revamp the financial services industry.
* American oil companies are finding resistance from the U.S., which is increasingly threatening economic sanctions, for business done overseas.
